title: BDI agents in social simulations: a survey
publisher: Cambridge University Press (The Knowledge Engineering Review, vol. 31, issue 3, pp. 207–238)

key_points.claim: Agent-based modelling displaced equation-based approaches. Model complexity is debated between KISS (Axelrod) and KIDS.
key_points.evidence_quote: Axelrod promoted the KISS principle: ‘Keep It Simple, Stupid’. But the community is divided and a new principle appeared: KIDS, ‘Keep It Descriptive, Stupid’.

key_points.claim: Agent cognition is still often modelled with simple reactive agents, which is inadequate for social science questions about human behaviour.
key_points.evidence_quote: agent cognition still tends to be modelled with simple reactive particle-like agents. This is not always appropriate

key_points.claim: BDI (belief-desire-intention) agents use folk-psychology concepts. This makes simulations easier for modellers and users to understand.
key_points.evidence_quote: an expressive paradigm using concepts from folk psychology, making it easier for modellers and users to understand the simulation

key_points.claim: The paper is a methodological guide to using BDI agents in social simulation. It also reviews existing methodologies and tools.
key_points.evidence_quote: This paper provides a methodological guide to the use of BDI agents in social simulations, and an overview of existing methodologies and tools for using them.

reliability_notes: Abstract only. The full text is a PDF that was not retrieved. It is a peer-reviewed survey by Benoit Gaudou and colleagues. The relevant aspect is agent cognition.
